records.subject: Checking in on Granite Ventures' setup
records.body:
Hi Sam,

How's Wrenfield treating you this week? If there's a specific workflow you're trying to replicate from your old tool, I'm happy to help map it over.

Thanks,
Chidi Haddad

records.subject: A better way to track team projects
records.body:
Hi Sam,

If you haven't had a chance to set up your first project yet, now's a great time -- it's the quickest way to see what Wrenfield is for.

Warmly,
Elena Kelly

records.subject: You're in -- let's get Granite Ventures set up
records.body:
Hi Sam,

Thanks for signing up for Wrenfield. Two things that help teams get going: create a project, and invite at least one teammate from Account Settings -> Members.

Happy to answer anything.

Thanks,
Chidi Haddad

records.text: :tada: New signup: *Granite Ventures* just joined on the starter plan!

decisions.rationale: Account is 6 days old, reached first project on day 2 (self-serve momentum), but no invite and no key milestone, with 8 days left. No customer reply to three outreach emails (75f115d5, 38a84ce4, 4c922322) and zero tickets suggests low engagement since setup, so unaided activation is possible but below even odds.

draft.subject: One next step for Granite Ventures
draft.body:
Hi Sam,

Nice work getting your first project up in Wrenfield last week. Projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them, so adding the real work there is usually the fastest way to see whether it fits how Granite Ventures runs.

The other piece most teams find useful is a teammate alongside you -- a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time, and teammates can be bulk-invited from a CSV file instead of one at a time.

Want me to walk through your next step on a short call this week?

Best,
Chidi
